question.problem: Given that the continuous random variable $X$ is uniformly distributed on the interval $[-7,3],$ compute $P(-5<X\le 1).$
question.worked_solution:
The probability density function for a uniformly distributed continuous random variable $X$ on an interval $[a,b]$ is given by

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{b-a},\, & a\le x\le b, \\ 0,\, & \text{otherwise.}\end{aligned}
$$

Our random variable $X$ is uniformly distributed on the interval $[-7,3],$ so it has the following probability density function:

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{10},\, & -7\le x\le 3, \\ 0,\, & \text{otherwise.}\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(-5<X\le 1) & ={\int }_{-5}^{1}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-5}^{1}\frac{1}{10}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1-(-5)}{10} \\  & =\frac{3}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$
